article.title: Ben Simmons’ NBA comeback derailed after tearing achilles tendon in practice
article.summary: Kings guard to undergo surgery and miss start of NBA season Former No 1 draft pick has been attempting to revive his career Ben Simmons’ comeback attempt is over before the start of the NBA regular season after he suffered a devastating injury at practice.…
article.content: Kings guard to undergo surgery and miss start of NBA season Former No 1 draft pick has been attempting to revive his career Ben Simmons’ comeback attempt is over before the start of the NBA regular season after he suffered a devastating injury at practice. The Australian tore his right achilles tendon during a live drill just three days out from Sacramento’s season opener against the Los Angeles Clippers and will undergo surgery. The 30-year-old had signed a one-year deal with the Kings in an attempt to revive a career ravaged by a series of significant injury setbacks and had shown promising flashes in pre-season, including a productive 26 minutes in a loss to San Antonio. article.aiArticle:
The latest attempt by **Ben Simmons** to re-establish his career in professional basketball has been abruptly halted before the regular season could even begin. According to **Sport | The Guardian**, the Sacramento Kings guard suffered a torn Achilles tendon during a team practice session, an injury that will force him to undergo immediate surgery and sidelines him indefinitely. 

This setback represents another major hurdle for the former number one draft pick, who has spent recent years trying to regain his footing in the league following multiple physical ailments. The publication notes that Simmons was actively working to revive his professional trajectory with the Kings organization prior to this training mishap. Medical staff have scheduled the necessary operation to repair the tendon, though no definitive timeline for his return to the hardwood has been released by the franchise.

## Background on Career Struggles

Injuries have heavily impacted the timeline of the veteran playmaker, who initially entered the league with immense expectations as a top selection in the draft. Over recent seasons, persistent health concerns have limited his playing time and complicated his stints with various franchises, making every attempted return a heavily scrutinized process for both analysts and supporters. 

From a broader perspective, severe lower-limb injuries like an Achilles tear carry profound implications for elite athletes whose games rely heavily on lateral quickness and explosive movement. When a prominent player faces such a lengthy rehabilitation process, the financial and competitive stakes are high for both the individual and the franchise, which must adjust its roster construction and tactical approach on the fly. For athletes attempting to rebuild their market value and prove their durability, missing extended stretches of competitive action adds immense pressure to an already challenging recovery road.

## What to Watch Next

Observers will be monitoring the Sacramento Kings' backcourt rotation to see how the coaching staff adjusts its lineup in the absence of the injured guard as the regular season tips off. Further updates from the team's medical department following the upcoming surgery will likely clarify the anticipated recovery duration and whether the organization plans to seek roster reinforcements. In the meantime, fans watching other sports leagues can keep track of alternative storylines, such as how [Iwobi delivers Fulham's first win of season](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/iwobi-deliver-fulhams-first-win-of-season) in European football.

Sources: [Sport | The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/19/ben-simmons-nba-comeback-derailed-after-tearing-achilles-tendon-in-practice)
